info.title: iBubbl API
info.description:
The iBubbl REST API. Send iMessages, manage contacts, and subscribe to webhook events from your backend.

Authenticate every request with a Bearer API key (`ib_pk_<hex>`) — generate one from your dashboard's API Access settings. See the [Authentication](/authentication) guide.

post.description:
Send a message to one contact (`contact_id`, or `to` — an E.164 phone number; the contact is created on first use), into an existing group (`chat_guid`), or to a new group (`participant_phones`). Exactly one of the four is required.

The response returns immediately with `status: "pending"` or `"queued"`. Delivery progress arrives as [webhook events](/webhooks/events) (`message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.read`, `message.failed`), or poll `GET /v1/messages/{id}`.

**Idempotency is required.** Provide a unique `idempotency_key` per logical send (UUIDv4 recommended); a retry with the same key and payload replays the original response, while a reused key with a different payload returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. See the [Idempotency](/idempotency) guide.

A send to an opted-out contact returns `422 contact_opted_out`; see [Suppression](/concepts/suppression).

To send files, list up to 10 `https` URLs or uploaded file IDs (`POST /v1/files`) in `attachments` (1:1 only); `body`, if set, is their caption. iBubbl downloads URLs before answering, which can take up to about 30 seconds, so allow 60 seconds before your client times out. See [Attachments](/guides/attachments).

On a `5xx` (including a `502`/`503` from the network edge during a deploy), retry with the same `idempotency_key`.

404.description: `not_found` (no contact with that `contact_id`), `group_not_found` (no group with that `chat_guid`), or `file_not_found` (an `attachments` file ID that isn't yours, or was deleted).

409.description: Idempotency key reused with a different payload.

422.description: Request rejected; see `detail.error`. `validation_error` (bad request shape), `contact_opted_out`, `contact_blocked`, `no_eligible_line`, `unresponsive_contact`, `cold_cap_exhausted`, `followup_cap_exhausted`, `daily_cap_exhausted`, `group_outbound_blocked_suppression`, `insufficient_participants`, `reply_target_not_found`, `reply_target_unsent`, `reply_target_partly_unsent`, `first_message_needs_text`, `attachment_fetch_failed`, `attachment_too_large`, `unsupported_attachment`, `attachment_combination_not_supported`, or `file_expired`.

429.description: `rate_limited`: too many sends with attachments are being downloaded right now. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry with the same `idempotency_key`.

500.description: `no_owner_rep` (your account has no active owner rep to send as) or `internal_error`. Retry with the same `idempotency_key`.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description:
List your messages, inbound and outbound, newest first. Use it to catch up after your webhook endpoint was down, or to read a conversation's history.

Results are paginated: `has_more` tells you whether there is another page, and you get it by passing the `id` of the last message as `starting_after`. Pages are stable while new messages arrive: nothing is skipped or repeated. See [Pagination](/concepts/pagination).

Filters combine with AND. A filter value that matches nothing (including another account's `contact_id` or `chat_guid`) returns an empty page. An unknown or repeated query parameter returns `422 validation_error`.

Messages stay listed after their contact is deleted or blocked.

Lists allow 120 requests a minute per account, across all your API keys and all lists. Over that, the answer is `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.
schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: starting_after

schema.description: The `id` of the last item on the page you already have. Returns the items that come after it, in the same order. Leave it out for the first page. An `id` that isn't one of yours returns `422 invalid_cursor`.

schema.description: Only messages with this contact: the 1:1 conversation, plus group messages they sent or that were addressed to them as the group's primary contact. For one whole conversation, use `conversation_id`.

422.description: `validation_error` (a bad, unknown or repeated query parameter, or `limit` outside 1–100) or `invalid_cursor` (`starting_after` is not one of your messages).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 120 list requests in 60 seconds from your account (all keys and all lists count together). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description:
Fetch a single message by its ID. Useful for polling the current delivery state when you can't subscribe to webhooks.

Returns `404 not_found` for both missing messages and messages owned by a different customer — existence is not leaked across tenants.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Send one of the six iMessage tapbacks (`love`, `like`, `dislike`, `laugh`, `emphasize`, `question`) on a message you received. It goes out over iMessage, or RCS for an Android contact; it can't go out by SMS.

The tapback is accepted as `pending`. When it reaches the contact's phone, `message.reaction.added` fires with `direction: "outbound"`. If it can't be sent, `message.reaction.failed` fires with a `failed_reason`.

One tapback per message, as in iMessage: a different type replaces your previous one (`message.reaction.removed` fires for it if it was sent). Sending the type that's already on the message answers `200` with that reaction and sends nothing.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

200.description: That tapback is already on the message; nothing sent.

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

422.description: `validation_error` (bad body, unknown `type`), `invalid_target` (a message you sent), `contact_blocked`, `contact_opted_out`, `sms_not_supported` (the message came in by SMS, or the conversation is going out by SMS), `target_unsent` or `target_partly_unsent` (the contact unsent the message, or part of it), `no_eligible_line` (the line it came in on is no longer active on your account; don't retry).

503.description: `opt_out_check_unavailable`: the contact's opt-out couldn't be checked, so nothing was sent. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description:
Take back a tapback you sent. It's removed from the contact's phone, and `message.reaction.removed` fires when that happens. Only a tapback from you, on this message, can be removed.

Idempotent: removing one already removed (or replaced, or failed) answers `200` with it unchanged.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

422.description: `target_unsent` or `target_partly_unsent`: the contact unsent the message, so the tapback can't be changed. `no_eligible_line`: the line it came in on is no longer active on your account; don't retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Change the text of a message you sent over iMessage, within 14 minutes 30 seconds of `sent_at` and up to five times, as on an iPhone.

The edit is accepted with `edit_status: "pending"`, and `body` shows the new text at once. When it reaches the recipient, `message.edited` fires with `direction: "outbound"` and `edit_count` goes up by one. If it doesn't, `message.edit_failed` fires and `body` goes back to the text they have.

On iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1, macOS 13 Ventura, visionOS 1 and later the message changes in place and is marked Edited. On earlier versions the recipient gets a follow-up message starting "Edited to" with the new text, and the original stays. In a group, only members using iMessage see the edit.

Sending the text the message already has answers `200` and changes nothing, so a retried request never spends a second edit.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

200.description: The message already has this text; nothing changed.

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

409.description: `edit_in_flight` (your previous edit hasn't reached the recipient yet; retry in a few seconds) or `already_unsent`.

422.description: `validation_error` (bad body), `invalid_target` (a message you received), `sms_not_supported` (it went out by SMS), `not_sent_yet` (still waiting to go out: cancel it instead), `not_editable` (no text to edit, or it failed or never went out), `edit_window_expired`, `edit_limit_reached`, `link_changed`, `contact_blocked`, `contact_opted_out`, `no_eligible_line` (the line it was sent from is no longer active on your account; don't retry).

503.description: `opt_out_check_unavailable`: the contact's opt-out couldn't be checked, so nothing was changed. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Take back a message you sent over iMessage, within 110 seconds of `sent_at` (iMessage allows two minutes).

The Undo Send is accepted with `unsend_status: "pending"`, and `body` is empty at once. When it reaches the recipient, `message.unsent` fires with `direction: "outbound"`. If it doesn't, `message.unsend_failed` fires and `body` comes back.

On iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1, macOS 13 Ventura, visionOS 1 and later the message disappears and both sides see a note that it was unsent. On earlier versions the original stays in the conversation: never rely on Undo Send to retract sensitive information.

A message with text and a link preview card (sent with `link_preview: true`, or typed in the dashboard) is two bubbles; both are unsent. A message with files (text and files, or several files) can't be unsent through the API (`422 multi_part`).

Repeating the request while the Undo Send is pending or done answers `200` and changes nothing; after `message.unsend_failed` it tries again, if it's still within the window.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

200.description: Already unsent or being unsent; nothing changed.

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

409.description: `edit_in_flight`: an edit of this message hasn't reached the recipient yet. Retry in a few seconds.

422.description: `invalid_target` (a message you received), `sms_not_supported` (it went out by SMS), `not_sent_yet` (still waiting to go out: cancel it instead), `not_unsendable` (it failed or never went out), `unsend_window_expired`, `multi_part`, `no_eligible_line` (the line it was sent from is no longer active on your account; don't retry).

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Stop a message you sent that hasn't gone out yet: one waiting for the contact's working hours or the line's hourly limit (`status: "pending"` with a `held_reason`), or queued by a capacity hold (`status: "queued"`). It moves to `cancelled`, will never be sent, and `message.cancelled` fires.

A message that is already being sent can't be stopped (`409 message_dispatching`); it goes out, and `message.sent` fires. Retrying the original `POST /v1/messages` with the same `idempotency_key` returns the cancelled message and doesn't send it again.

Idempotent: cancelling a cancelled message answers `200` with it, and no second webhook fires.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

409.description: `message_dispatching`: it is already being sent and can't be stopped.

422.description: `not_cancellable`: not a message of yours that is still waiting to go out (it was sent, failed or expired, or it is a message you received).

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Upload one file to send in messages: a `multipart/form-data` body with one part named `file`. The answer is a file object; put its `id` in the `attachments` of `POST /v1/messages`, alone or with `https` URLs.

The same types and sizes as URL attachments: images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF) and GIFs up to 25 MiB, MP4/MOV video up to 50 MiB, PDF up to 10 MB, audio (MP3, M4A, AAC) up to 25 MiB. A file is refused as soon as it breaks a rule, and its content must match its type.

A file can be sent any number of times until `expires_at`, 24 hours after the upload; then it is deleted. Each send keeps its own copy, so deleting a file never touches messages already sent. An account holds at most 500 files and 1 GiB of uploads at once.

Uploads take no idempotency key: a retried upload stores a second file (the unused one expires). Uploads allow 60 requests a minute and 4 at once per account; over that, the answer is `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. See [Send attachments](/guides/attachments).

408.description: `upload_timeout`: the body took over 300 seconds, or paused for over 30. Nothing was stored.

422.description: Nothing was stored. `validation_error` (not multipart, no part named `file`, another part, two files, an empty file, or a cut-off body), `unsupported_attachment` (a type that can't be sent, or content that doesn't match its type), `attachment_too_large` (over its type's cap), or `file_quota_exceeded` (the account holds too many uploads).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 60 uploads in 60 seconds from your account (all keys count together; other requests have their own budgets). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

file.description: The file. Its type is the part's `Content-Type`, or, when that is missing or `application/octet-stream`, the file name's extension. Its name becomes the name the recipient sees.

get.description: Fetch an uploaded file's details by ID: its name, type, size and when it expires. The contents are not returned. Returns `404 file_not_found` once the file has expired or been deleted.

404.description: `file_not_found`: no file with that ID on your account, or it expired or was deleted.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description: Delete an uploaded file before it expires. Messages already sent with it keep their own copy. A later send naming it returns `404 file_not_found`.

404.description: `file_not_found`: no file with that ID on your account, or it expired or was deleted.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Upsert a contact by E.164 phone number. Returns `201 Created` on a new contact, `200 OK` on an existing match. A number whose only match is a deleted contact creates a new contact.

Optional fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `city`, `state`, `timezone`) apply only when the existing record's value is null — values set previously by a rep or by a prior API call are preserved. This protects human-edited data from being clobbered by automation; to overwrite, use `PATCH /v1/contacts/{id}`.

`tags` only ever adds tags. Every value is checked before anything is saved.

If `timezone` is provided, it must be one of the 20 supported IANA timezones (US, Canada, and a few international zones such as `Europe/London`); anything else returns `422 invalid_timezone`.

A new contact for a number that opted out earlier (for example, one you deleted after an opt-out) starts with `opted_out: true`.

422.description: `validation_error` (bad request shape, `phone` not E.164, an unknown field), `invalid_timezone`, `invalid_email`, `invalid_tag` or `duplicate_tag`.

500.description: `internal_error`: a tag was deleted twice while it was being added. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description:
List your contacts, newest first. Deleted contacts are never listed.

Results are paginated: `has_more` tells you whether there is another page, and you get it by passing the `id` of the last contact as `starting_after`. Pages are stable while contacts are added: nothing is skipped or repeated. See [Pagination](/concepts/pagination).

Filters combine with AND. A filter value that matches nothing (including a tag you don't have) returns an empty page. An unknown or repeated query parameter returns `422 validation_error`.

Lists allow 120 requests a minute per account, across all your API keys and all lists. Over that, the answer is `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

schema.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: search

schema.description: Only contacts matching every word, case-insensitively, as part of the first name, last name, email or phone number: `sam rivera` finds Sam Rivera. A word written like a phone number also matches by its digits, so `415-555-1234` finds `+14155551234`. The characters `"`, `\` and `*` are ignored. Up to 100 characters.

A word written like a phone number also matches by its digits, so `415-555-1234` finds `+14155551234`. The characters `"`, `\` and `*` are ignored. Up to 100 characters.

parameters.name: opted_out

schema.description: `true`: only opted-out contacts. `false`: only the others.
schema.title: Opted Out

parameters.description: `true`: only opted-out contacts. `false`: only the others.

parameters.name: blocked

schema.description: `true`: only blocked contacts. `false`: only the others.
schema.title: Blocked

parameters.description: `true`: only blocked contacts. `false`: only the others.

parameters.name: tag

schema.description: Only contacts with this tag, matched trimmed and case-insensitively (`vip` matches `VIP`).
schema.title: Tag

parameters.description: Only contacts with this tag, matched trimmed and case-insensitively (`vip` matches `VIP`).

422.description: `validation_error` (a bad, unknown or repeated query parameter, `limit` outside 1–100, or a `search` with nothing to match) or `invalid_cursor` (`starting_after` is not one of your contacts).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 120 list requests in 60 seconds from your account (all keys and all lists count together). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description: Fetch a single contact by ID. Returns `404 not_found` for both missing contacts and contacts owned by a different customer — existence is not leaked across tenants.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

patch.description:
Overwrite the fields you send. Fields you leave out are not touched; a field sent as `null` is cleared. Unlike the upsert, this replaces values a rep set.

`phone` can't be changed. Tags have their own endpoints.

422.description: `validation_error` (bad request shape or an unknown field, including `phone` and `tags`), `invalid_timezone` or `invalid_email`.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description:
Delete a contact. It disappears from the list and from `GET /v1/contacts/{id}`, and every endpoint that takes its `id` (including `POST /v1/messages` with `contact_id`) returns `404 not_found`. Deleting it again also returns `404`.

What stays: its messages and conversations, which `GET /v1/messages` still lists under the old `contact_id`; messages already accepted for it and still waiting, which still go out (cancel them in the dashboard to stop them); and its opt-out, which belongs to the number.

Upserting the same number, sending to it with `to`, or an inbound message from it creates a **new** contact with a new `id`. Names, tags and a block are not carried over; an opt-out is.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.summary: Add a tag to a contact
post.description: Add one tag. Idempotent: a tag the contact already has answers `200` unchanged. The name matches an existing tag trimmed and case-insensitively; a new name creates the tag. A newly added tag can start workflows with a "Tag added" trigger.

422.description: `validation_error` (bad request shape or an unknown field), `invalid_tag` or `duplicate_tag`.

500.description: `internal_error`: a tag was deleted twice while it was being added. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a contact
delete.description: Remove a tag by name (URL-encode it), matched trimmed and case-insensitively. Idempotent: a tag the contact doesn't have answers `200` unchanged. Removing a tag starts no workflow.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Record that this person opted out of messages, as a STOP reply does. **This can't be undone**, through the API or the dashboard: every later send to this number answers `422 contact_opted_out`, even after the contact is deleted and created again.

The first opt-out fires a `contact.opted_out` webhook with `source: "api"`. New sends are refused from then on, but a message accepted earlier and still waiting (held for sending hours, or queued) can still go out; cancel it in the dashboard to stop it.

Idempotent: a contact already opted out (in any way) answers `200` with its current state, and no second webhook fires.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
A block is yours, on this contact: sends to them return `422 contact_blocked` (group conversations they're in are not affected). Their inbound messages are still stored and still fire `message.inbound`, but don't mark the conversation unread, notify anyone or start workflows. Unlike an opt-out, a block fires no webhook and can be undone with `DELETE /v1/contacts/{id}/block`. A contact deleted and created again starts unblocked.

Idempotent: blocking a blocked contact answers `200` and keeps the original `blocked_at`.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description:
Undo a block: sends to this contact are accepted again. An opt-out is not affected.

Idempotent: unblocking a contact that isn't blocked answers `200` unchanged.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Mark every message you've received in this conversation read. It clears the unread badge in the iBubbl inbox and, when read receipts are on for your account, sends the contact a read receipt: they see "Read" under their latest message on iMessage, and on RCS (Android). SMS has no read receipts.

A receipt goes out only when there was something unread, and never to a group, a blocked contact or one who opted out. `read_receipt` says whether one was queued, and why not.

Idempotent: calling again with nothing new answers `200` with `marked_count: 0`.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Show the contact the typing bubble (the three dots) in this conversation. It lasts 10 seconds: call again every 5 seconds to keep it going. Sending a message clears it on the contact's phone; so does `DELETE`, or simply not calling again.

Typing shows only in a 1:1 iMessage conversation the contact has already messaged. Anywhere else the call answers `200` with `status: "ignored"` and an `ignored_reason`, and does nothing.

Typing is a signal to the contact, so it's refused for a blocked contact or one who opted out.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account); calls closer than 3 seconds apart are answered without doing anything new.

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

422.description: `contact_blocked`, `contact_opted_out`, or `no_eligible_line` (the line this conversation is on is no longer active on your account; don't retry).

503.description: `opt_out_check_unavailable`: the contact's opt-out couldn't be checked, so typing wasn't shown. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description:
Stop showing the typing bubble. You don't need this before sending: a sent message clears it on its own. Some phones keep showing the bubble for up to a minute after a stop that isn't followed by a message.

Typing shows only in a 1:1 iMessage conversation the contact has already messaged. Anywhere else the call answers `200` with `status: "ignored"` and an `ignored_reason`, and does nothing.

Idempotent: stopping when nothing is typing answers `200` `stopped`.

Counts toward the conversation-actions rate limit (300 a minute per account).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 300 conversation actions in 60 seconds from your account (all keys, and tapbacks, read, typing, edit, unsend and cancel requests, count together; list requests have their own budget). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description:
List your lines, newest first: each line's number, status, whether it is online, and today's usage against its send limits. Retired lines stay listed, so the `line_id` on an older message always resolves.

The counts are live: read them before a batch of first messages to new contacts to see how many the line can still take today and this hour. See [Limits and queues](/concepts/limits).

Results are paginated like every list: pass the `id` of the last line as `starting_after` while `has_more` is true. See [Pagination](/concepts/pagination). An unknown or repeated query parameter returns `422 validation_error`.

Lists allow 120 requests a minute per account, across all your API keys and all lists. Over that, the answer is `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.
schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: starting_after

schema.description: The `id` of the last item on the page you already have. Returns the items that come after it, in the same order. Leave it out for the first page. An `id` that isn't one of yours returns `422 invalid_cursor`.
schema.title: Starting After

parameters.description: The `id` of the last item on the page you already have. Returns the items that come after it, in the same order. Leave it out for the first page. An `id` that isn't one of yours returns `422 invalid_cursor`.

503.description: `limits_unavailable`: an active line's limit counters couldn't be read. Nothing is wrong with the line; try again shortly.

422.description: `validation_error` (a bad, unknown or repeated query parameter, or `limit` outside 1–100) or `invalid_cursor` (`starting_after` is not one of your lines).

429.description: `rate_limited`: more than 120 list requests in 60 seconds from your account (all keys and all lists count together). Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description: Fetch one of your lines by ID, with today's usage against its send limits. Use it to look up the `line_id` on a message. Returns `404 line_not_found` for an ID that isn't one of your lines.

503.description: `limits_unavailable`: an active line's limit counters couldn't be read. Nothing is wrong with the line; try again shortly.

404.description: `line_not_found`: no line with that ID on your account.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.description:
Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive events. The response includes the signing secret **once** — store it immediately; it cannot be retrieved again. Use the secret to verify incoming webhook signatures (see [Signature verification](/guides/webhook-signatures)).

If `event_types` is omitted, the subscription receives all event types. You can register multiple subscriptions per account (e.g., one for production, one for staging).

Delivery is at-least-once with exponential backoff. Customer endpoints should be idempotent based on the event `id`.

422.description: `invalid_url` (URL is not HTTPS) or `validation_error` (for example an unknown event type).

500.description: `internal_error`: the subscription could not be saved. Retry.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description: Returns all currently active webhook subscriptions for the authenticated customer. Revoked subscriptions are omitted — query them by ID directly (`GET /v1/webhooks/{id}`) if you need their history.

schema.title: Response V1 List Webhooks V1 Webhooks Get

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

get.description: Fetch a single subscription by ID. Returns the subscription regardless of revoked status (so you can inspect history). `404 not_found` is returned for both missing subscriptions and those owned by a different customer.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

delete.description:
Soft-revoke a subscription. After revocation, no further events are delivered to its URL. The row is retained for audit purposes; you can still fetch it with `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}` and see its `revoked_at` timestamp.

Revoking an already-revoked subscription is a no-op that returns `{"status": "already_revoked"}`.

403.description: `forbidden`: your iBubbl account is suspended or cancelled.

post.summary: Receive an event from a connected app
post.description:
Receive a webhook from a connected third-party app (for example Recharge) and start any workflow whose **Webhook received** trigger matches it.

The URL you paste into the sending app carries its own credential, so this endpoint takes no `Authorization` header. Create a source in **Settings → Inbound events** to get the full URL; the token is shown once.

**Any app (secret URL)** sources need no signature: the URL is the credential, so keep it private. They accept JSON or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies and at most 60 requests a minute. Beyond that the answer is `429` while a workflow is listening on the source; with none listening, the event is accepted and dropped.

**Signed** sources must sign every request. For Recharge, that is the `X-Recharge-Hmac-Sha256` header computed with your **API Client Secret** — which is not the same value as your API token. An unsigned or mis-signed request returns `403 invalid_signature`.

**Redeliveries are safe.** Providers resend events, and Recharge's dunning fires one event per charge retry. Each workflow's `event_id_path` identifies the underlying object, so repeat deliveries of the same event fold onto the run that already exists rather than messaging the customer again.

A `200` means the event was accepted, not that it matched anything — check `runs_started`, and see the source's status in Settings when it is unexpectedly `0`.

403.description: Signature missing or does not match.

404.description: No such source, or it has been revoked.

429.description: Secret-URL source over its limit of 60 requests a minute, while a workflow is listening on it.

detail.description: Error envelope. Every `/v1` error response wraps a stable `error` code and a human-readable `message` in `detail`.

detail.message: Exactly one of contact_id, to, chat_guid, or participant_phones is required

error.title: Error
error.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Use this for branching logic in your integration; the human-readable `message` is subject to change. See the Error Reference for the catalog.

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.
examples: Exactly one of contact_id, to, chat_guid, or participant_phones is required

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Contact's phone number as first seen. Usually E.164; a contact first created by an inbound SMS can carry the sender's bare national form (e.g. `4155551234`). Upserting any form of the same number returns this contact.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone used for this contact's sending hours, or null if not set yet. When it is null and the number is a US or Canadian one, iBubbl infers the zone from the area code and saves it here when the contact's first message is processed; otherwise your account's timezone is used. Once set, an upsert never replaces it, so pass `timezone` on the first upsert, before you send, or change it with PATCH.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: The contact's tag names, sorted case-insensitively.

opted_out.title: Opted Out
opted_out.description: True if this person has opted out: a STOP reply, a rep in the dashboard, a Do Not Disturb in your connected GoHighLevel account, or `POST /v1/contacts/{id}/opt-out`. When true, every send to this contact returns `422 contact_opted_out`. An opt-out can't be undone, and it belongs to the number: a contact deleted and created again is still opted out.

opted_out_at.title: Opted Out At
opted_out_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the opt-out, or null.

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.description: True if you blocked this contact (dashboard or `POST /v1/contacts/{id}/block`). Sends to them return `422 contact_blocked` until you unblock them. Unlike an opt-out, a block is yours to undo, and it fires no webhook.

blocked_at.title: Blocked At
blocked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the block, or null.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the contact was created.

data.title: Data
data.description: Up to `limit` contacts, newest first: by `created_at`, then by `id` for contacts created in the same microsecond.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more contacts match after the last one in `data`. To get them, repeat the request with `starting_after` set to that contact's `id`.

marked_count.title: Marked Count
marked_count.description: How many received messages this call marked read (0 if they already were).

read_receipt.title: Read Receipt
read_receipt.description: `queued`: the contact will see "Read" (iMessage, and RCS on Android). `skipped`: no receipt goes out; see `read_receipt_skipped_reason`.

read_receipt_skipped_reason.title: Read Receipt Skipped Reason
read_receipt_skipped_reason.description: Why no receipt: `nothing_unread` (nothing new since the last read), `receipts_off` (read receipts are off for your account), `group` (never sent in group conversations), `contact_blocked`, `contact_opted_out`, `opt_out_check_unavailable` (the opt-out couldn't be checked, so none was sent), or `line_inactive` (the line this conversation is on is no longer active on your account). Null when queued.

received.title: Received
received.description: Always `true` once the signature has been verified.

runs_started.title: Runs Started
runs_started.description: How many workflow runs this event started. `0` is a normal answer — it means no active workflow's trigger matched, or this event was a redelivery that de-duplicated onto an existing run.

phone_number.title: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The line's phone number in E.164 format.

status.title: Status
status.description: `active` = sends and receives messages. `paused` = temporarily not sending; new messages to its contacts go out on another of your active lines. `retired` = no longer yours to send from; it stays listed so the `line_id` on older messages still resolves.

online.title: Online
online.description: For an `active` line: whether the line has checked in with iBubbl in the last 2 minutes. `false` means new messages wait as `queued` until it is back. It says nothing about any one recipient. Null for `paused` and `retired` lines.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, with microseconds and a `Z`, of when the line was set up. Lists sort by it.

limits.description: Today's usage against the line's send limits, read live. Null for `paused` and `retired` lines, and for an active line that isn't on the published limits (ask support if you see one).

used.title: Used
used.description: New contacts the line messaged in the last 60 minutes.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The limit this line runs in any rolling 60 minutes. It can be lower than the published number while iBubbl has lowered this line's limits; it is never higher.

waiting.title: Waiting
waiting.description: Messages to new contacts waiting as `pending` with `held_reason: "hourly_limit"` for a slot to free.

next_slot_at.title: Next Slot At
next_slot_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the line can message a new contact again. Null while the hour has room, or when no estimate is possible.

used.title: Used
used.description: How much of the limit the line has used so far.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The limit this line runs today. It can be lower than the published number while iBubbl has lowered this line's limits; it is never higher.

resets_at.title: Resets At
resets_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the next midnight America/New_York, when `used` goes back to 0.

new_contacts_today.description: New contacts messaged since midnight America/New_York.

new_contacts_this_hour.description: New contacts messaged in the rolling 60 minutes.

messages_today.description: Every outbound message since midnight America/New_York, waiting and failed ones included; not `cancelled` or `expired` ones.

data.title: Data
data.description: Up to `limit` lines, newest first: by `created_at`, then by `id`.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more lines match after the last one in `data`. To get them, repeat the request with `starting_after` set to that line's `id`.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `outbound` = sent from your line (through the API, the dashboard or an automation); `inbound` = received from a contact. An inbound message has `status` `delivered`, or `read` once it has been read in the dashboard.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, with microseconds and a `Z`, of when iBubbl recorded the message. It never changes, so it is what `GET /v1/messages` sorts and filters by; pass it back as `created_after` / `created_before` unchanged.

status.title: Status
status.description: Lifecycle state. `pending` = accepted and on its way out; it may be waiting for the contact's working hours or the line's hourly limit for new contacts (see `held_until`). `queued` = parked by a capacity hold (`hourly_cap_hit` / `line_offline`), retried automatically. `sent` / `delivered` / `read` = delivery progression. `failed` = the send failed — see webhook `message.failed` for the reason; it can follow `sent` (or a `read` with no confirmed delivery) when iMessage reports the send failed after accepting it (`failed_reason` `imessage_undeliverable` / `imessage_error:<code>`), and such a message can still move to `delivered` / `read` if Apple later confirms it. `expired` = still queued after an hour, so dropped; it will not send. `cancelled` = stopped in the dashboard before it was sent; it will not send (webhook `message.cancelled`).

to.title: To
to.description: The contact's phone number (E.164) for 1:1 messages: the destination of an outbound message, and the sender of an inbound one. Null for group messages — the group is identified by `chat_guid` instead.

line_id.title: Line Id
line_id.description: ID of your line this message was on: the line that sent an outbound message, or received an inbound one. Group messages too. The same `id` as in `GET /v1/lines`.

line_number.title: Line Number
line_number.description: That line's phone number (E.164), the line's `phone_number` in `GET /v1/lines`. Unlike `to`, it is your side of the conversation, in both directions.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: ID of the contact this message was sent to. For groups, this is the 'primary' participant the message was addressed to (the first participant in `participant_phones` on a new group create); the conversation's full participant list is available via the conversation.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: ID of the conversation this message belongs to. Stable for the lifetime of the conversation; use it to fetch the thread or correlate webhook events.

conversation_kind.title: Conversation Kind
conversation_kind.description: `one_to_one` for sends to a single contact, `group` for iMessage groups (2+ participants in addition to your iBubbl line).

chat_guid.title: Chat Guid
chat_guid.description: Opaque identifier for the group chat (e.g. `any;+;<hex>`). Returned for `group` messages — use it to address later messages to the same group via the `chat_guid` request shape. Null for `one_to_one` messages, and for a brand-new group until the group has been created in iMessage (that happens when the first message goes out, which can wait for sending hours); poll `GET /v1/messages/{id}` to see it fill in. It changes when a participant is added to the group.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: How the message travelled: `imessage`, or `sms` (a text, including RCS). For an outbound message, how it actually went out (`sms` when the recipient couldn't be reached on iMessage); null until it has been sent. For an inbound message, how it arrived; null when that wasn't recorded.

sent_at.title: Sent At
sent_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Set when the message is accepted, then replaced by the actual send time once it goes out. Use `status` (`sent` / `delivered` / `read`), not `sent_at`, to tell whether it has actually gone out.

held_until.title: Held Until
held_until.description: While a `pending` message is being held, the expected time (ISO 8601 UTC) it will go out: the next opening of the contact's working hours; for `hourly_limit`, an estimate of when a slot frees. Recomputed within about 10 seconds. Null when the message is not held, when `held_reason` is `working_hours` but no sending day is enabled, and when it is `hourly_limit` with no estimate.

held_reason.title: Held Reason
held_reason.description: Why a `pending` message is being held right now: `working_hours` (outside the contact's working hours) or `hourly_limit` (the line has started its limit of new contacts for this hour; the message goes out by itself when a slot frees, at about `held_until`). Null when it is not held.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: The iMessage send effect requested for this message, or null. It shows on the recipient's device only when `channel` is `imessage`.

link_preview.title: Link Preview
link_preview.description: `true` when the message was sent through the API with `link_preview: true`. A message typed in the dashboard gets a preview card for its link without it, and shows `false`.

reply_to_message_id.title: Reply To Message Id
reply_to_message_id.description: The ID of the message this one quotes as an inline reply, or null. The quote shows on the recipient's device only when `channel` is `imessage`.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: The files on this message, in the order they were sent: sent with `attachments`, from the dashboard or an automation, or received from the contact. Empty when there are none. File contents and URLs are not returned.

edited_at.title: Edited At
edited_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the latest edit that reached the recipient: one of yours (`POST /v1/messages/{id}/edit`, or the dashboard), or, on an inbound message, the contact's own edit. Null when it was never edited.

edit_count.title: Edit Count
edit_count.description: How many of your edits reached the recipient. iMessage allows five per message. Always `0` on an inbound message.

edit_status.title: Edit Status
edit_status.description: `pending` = your latest edit is on its way (`body` already shows the new text); `failed` = it didn't reach the recipient, and `body` is back to the text they have (webhook `message.edit_failed`); `edited` = the message was edited. Null when it never was.

unsend_status.title: Unsend Status
unsend_status.description: `pending` = your Undo Send is on its way; `unsent` = the whole message was unsent (by you, or by the contact on an inbound message) and `body` is empty; `partly_unsent` = part of it was (its text, a link preview or a file); `failed` = your Undo Send didn't happen and the recipient still has the message (webhook `message.unsend_failed`). Null when nothing was unsent.

unsent_at.title: Unsent At
unsent_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the message (or the latest part of it) was unsent. Null unless `unsend_status` is `unsent` or `partly_unsent`.

example.body: Hey Sam — quick check-in about your order.

size_bytes.title: Size Bytes
size_bytes.description: Size in bytes. An inbound file can show `0` for a few seconds, until iBubbl has received it.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: The name the recipient sees: an upload's `filename`, or a URL file's name (its `Content-Disposition`, else the last part of its path). Null for received files, and for files sent before names were kept or without a usable name.

data.title: Data
data.description: Up to `limit` messages, newest first: by `created_at`, then by `id` for messages recorded in the same microsecond.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more messages match after the last one in `data`. To get them, repeat the request with `starting_after` set to that message's `id`.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: The message the tapback is on.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The conversation that message is in.

emoji.title: Emoji
emoji.description: The tapback as an emoji, e.g. `❤️`.

status.title: Status
status.description: `pending`: accepted, not yet on the contact's phone. `sent`: delivered to Messages (`message.reaction.added` fires then). `failed`: never sent, see `failed_reason` (`message.reaction.failed` fires). `removed`: you removed it, or a newer tapback of yours on the same message replaced it.

failed_reason.title: Failed Reason
failed_reason.description: Why a `failed` tapback wasn't sent: `sms_target`, `target_not_found`, `bb_rejected`, `messages_error`, `expired`, `retract_rejected` or `target_unsent`. Null otherwise.

removed_at.title: Removed At
removed_at.description: When it was removed or replaced (UTC); null while active.

typing.title: Typing
typing.description: Whether the typing bubble is on after this call.

status.title: Status
status.description: `started` (or kept going), `stopped`, or `ignored`: typing can't be shown here and nothing was done; see `ignored_reason`.

ignored_reason.title: Ignored Reason
ignored_reason.description: `group` (not available in group conversations), `not_imessage` (the contact is on SMS or RCS), `no_chat` (the contact hasn't messaged this line yet). Null otherwise.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the bubble stops unless you call again (UTC), 10 seconds after the call. Null unless `started`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Must look like an email address, or `422 invalid_email`.

state.title: State
state.description: Trimmed, a 2-letter code upper-cased; blank clears it.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: One of the supported IANA zones, or `422 invalid_timezone`. `null` returns the contact to automatic: iBubbl infers the zone from a US or Canadian area code again.

ContactUpdate.title: ContactUpdate
ContactUpdate.description: Only the fields you send change. Send a field as `null` to clear it. `phone` can't be changed, and tags have their own endpoints. Fields not listed here are rejected with `422 validation_error`.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Phone number in E.164 format (e.g. `+14155551234`). The unique key for contacts — upserting an existing phone returns the same contact ID.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.description: Contact's first name. Only applied if the existing record's `first_name` is null — rep-edited values are sticky and won't be overwritten by automation. To change it, use `PATCH /v1/contacts/{id}`.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: Contact's last name. Same sticky-update semantics as `first_name`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email address. Must look like one (`name@domain.tld`, no spaces), or the call returns `422 invalid_email`. Same sticky-update semantics as `first_name`.

city.title: City
city.description: City. Trimmed; blank is treated as not sent. Same sticky-update semantics as `first_name`.

state.title: State
state.description: State, province or region. Trimmed, and a 2-letter code is upper-cased (`ny` → `NY`). Same sticky-update semantics as `first_name`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone for working-hours scheduling. Must be one of the supported allowlist (US/Canada timezones, plus common international). Sends to this contact respect the timezone for outside-hours scheduling. Same sticky-update semantics as names.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Tag names to add, at most 20. Only ever adds: tags the contact already has are kept, and none are removed. A name matches an existing tag trimmed and case-insensitively (`vip` reuses `VIP`); a new name creates the tag. Each name is 1–64 characters with no invisible characters, or the call returns `422 invalid_tag` before anything is saved. A newly added tag can start workflows with a "Tag added" trigger.

ContactUpsert.title: ContactUpsert
ContactUpsert.description: Fields not listed here are rejected with `422 validation_error`.

id.title: Id
id.description: Unique file identifier: `file_` and 32 hex characters. Put it in a message's `attachments`, alone or with URLs.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: The name the recipient sees: the uploaded name without path, control characters or `/\:*?"<>|`, at most 100 characters before the extension, which is always the type's own (`.jpg`, `.pdf` ...). Null when the upload had no usable name; the file then goes out with a generated one.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the upload.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp 24 hours after the upload. Until then the file can be sent any number of times; after it, sends naming it return `422 file_expired` and the file is deleted.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: 1:1 send by existing contact ID (a UUID). Mutually exclusive with `to`, `chat_guid`, and `participant_phones`.

to.title: To
to.description: 1:1 send by E.164 phone number (e.g. `+14155551234`). If the number doesn't match an existing contact, one is created automatically. Mutually exclusive with `contact_id`, `chat_guid`, and `participant_phones`.

chat_guid.title: Chat Guid
chat_guid.description: Send into an existing iMessage group identified by its opaque `chat_guid` (e.g. `any;+;<hex>`). Webhook events don't carry it: read it from the response to a send into the group, or from `GET /v1/messages/{id}` for any message in the group (an inbound `message_id` works too). The value changes when a participant is added to the group; an old value then returns `404 group_not_found`. Mutually exclusive with `contact_id`, `to`, and `participant_phones`.

participant_phones.title: Participant Phones
participant_phones.description: Create a brand-new iMessage group and send the first message in one call. List of 2 or more E.164 phone numbers (your iBubbl line is added automatically; do not include it). Mutually exclusive with `contact_id`, `to`, and `chat_guid`. Optionally pair with `group_name` to set the group's display name.

group_name.title: Group Name
group_name.description: Display name for a new iMessage group. Only valid alongside `participant_phones`. Optional — iMessage will fall back to the participants' names if omitted.

body.title: Body
body.description:
The message text. Plain text only; emoji + Unicode are supported. For a line break, include a newline (`
` in the JSON string); use `
`, not `
`. A retry with the same `idempotency_key` must send the identical body, line breaks included, or it returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. Required unless `attachments` is set; with attachments it is sent as their caption, and it is required for the first message to a contact (`422 first_message_needs_text`).
examples: Hey Sam — quick check-in about your order.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Up to 10 files to send, in order: each an `https` URL iBubbl downloads when the request arrives, or the `id` of a file you uploaded with `POST /v1/files` (`file_` and 32 hex characters). Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF) and GIFs up to 25 MiB each, MP4/MOV video up to 50 MiB, PDF up to 10 MB, audio (MP3, M4A, AAC) up to 25 MiB on its own; 86 MB in all. With other files, audio must be one MP3 of at most 2 MB. The type comes from the response's `Content-Type` (or the URL's extension when that is `application/octet-stream`). A URL that can't be downloaded, or a file that breaks these rules, rejects the whole request (`422 attachment_fetch_failed`, `attachment_too_large`, `unsupported_attachment`, `attachment_combination_not_supported`) and nothing is sent. A file ID that isn't yours, or was deleted, is `404 file_not_found`; one past its `expires_at` is `422 file_expired`. Only with `to` or `contact_id`, and not with `effect` or `reply_to_message_id`. The items, in order, are part of the payload compared for idempotency; a replay never downloads or copies them again.

reply_to_message_id.title: Reply To Message Id
reply_to_message_id.description: Send as an inline reply that quotes an earlier message (a UUID: the `id` of a message, or the `message_id` of a `message.inbound` event). The message must be in the conversation you are sending to: the same contact for a 1:1 send, the same group for a `chat_guid` send; otherwise `422 reply_target_not_found`. A message the contact unsent returns `422 reply_target_unsent`, and one they unsent part of `422 reply_target_partly_unsent`. iMessage only: when the message goes out as SMS (see `channel`) it is sent as plain text, without the quote. Not allowed with `participant_phones` or `attachments`.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: An iMessage send effect. Bubble effects: `slam`, `loud`, `gentle`, `invisible` (Invisible Ink). Screen effects: `echo`, `spotlight`, `balloons`, `confetti`, `love`, `lasers`, `fireworks`, `celebration`, `shooting_star`. iMessage only: when the message goes out as SMS (see `channel`) it is sent without the effect. Not allowed with `participant_phones` or `attachments`.

link_preview.title: Link Preview
link_preview.description: Send the link with a preview card (the page's title and image), as when a person types it on an iPhone. Messages sent through the API are otherwise plain text. The body must end in exactly one http(s) link, with no other link in it; a body that is only the link is sent as the card alone, and text before the link goes as its own bubble, followed by the card. Your line opens the page to build the card when it sends the message, so a click-tracked link counts a click and a one-time link (a login or reset link, a single-use coupon) may be used up: don't set it for those. The card is built over iMessage, and over SMS or RCS where your line supports it. `to` or `contact_id` only, and not with `attachments`, `effect` or `reply_to_message_id`.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Client-supplied unique key per logical send. Keys never expire: reusing a key with the same payload replays the original message, however long ago it was sent, and the same key with a different payload returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. The one exception is a message that ended `failed` or `expired`: its key is released and the retry is sent as a new message. The payload compared is the routing field exactly as sent (`to`, `contact_id`, `chat_guid`, or the sorted `participant_phones` plus `group_name`), `body`, and `effect`, `reply_to_message_id` and `attachments` when set, so a retry that switches from `to` to the same contact's `contact_id` is a 409. Generate a new UUIDv4 for every distinct message.

MessageCreate.title: MessageCreate
MessageCreate.description: Fields not listed here are ignored without an error: the request still succeeds and they are not stored.

example.body: Hey Sam — quick check-in about your order.

body.title: Body
body.description: The new text. It replaces the whole text of the message; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed. For a message that went out with a link preview, keep the link exactly as sent and at the end, and change only the text before it. Fields not listed here are rejected with `422 validation_error`.

type.title: Type
type.description: One of the six iMessage tapbacks: `love`, `like`, `dislike`, `laugh`, `emphasize`, `question`. Custom emoji tapbacks can't be sent. Fields not listed here are rejected with `422 validation_error`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Tag name, 1–64 characters with no invisible characters. Matches an existing tag trimmed and case-insensitively; a new name creates the tag.

url.title: Url
url.description: HTTPS URL that will receive webhook POST requests. HTTP is rejected (`422 invalid_url`).

event_types.title: Event Types
event_types.description: Filter to a specific subset of events. Omit, or pass `null` or `[]`, to receive ALL event types, including ones added later. Every entry must be a type from the [Webhook Events catalog](/webhooks/events); an unknown type returns `422 validation_error`.

status.title: Status
status.description: `revoked` if this call performed the revocation; `already_revoked` if the subscription was already revoked.

secret_prefix.title: Secret Prefix
secret_prefix.description: First 14 characters of the signing secret (`whsec_` + 8 hex). Useful for identifying which subscription's secret is in use without revealing the full value. The full secret is returned only once, at creation time.

event_types.title: Event Types
event_types.description: Event filter, or null if subscribed to all events.

last_delivered_at.title: Last Delivered At
last_delivered_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent successful delivery to this subscription, or null if no event has been delivered yet.

revoked_at.title: Revoked At
revoked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the subscription was revoked, or null if active. Revoked subscriptions stop receiving events.
